title: Clarify catalog admission contracts and compatibility lifecycle for community/open models
creator: Maya R. Patel
description: Clarify the acceptance contract and lifecycle for admitting community / open-source models into the Redwood catalog. This ticket consolidates open questions from PRD review: the exact metadata we require for an entry, minimum runtime compatibility signals, when and how to enforce version pinning, and a bounded upgrade/rollback policy. Goal: produce a short, actionable admission checklist and a compatibility annotation schema that runtime and onboarding teams can validate automatically.
background: Over the last 9 months we've had repeated friction between runtime engineers and PMs when new open models land in the catalog: missing runtime flags, incompatible kernel paths, unexpected memory characteristics, and unclear pinning semantics. Current intake forms are high level; eng teams end up creating ad-hoc compatibility notes in PRs. This causes production incidents and slows adoption of community weights. We need a repeatable contract so catalog entries are predictable for Dedicated and Private deployments.
scope_clarifications: In-scope: define the minimal metadata and compatibility annotations required for new catalog entries; decide when pinning is mandatory vs advisory; acceptance criteria for automated sanity tests used by intake; rollback and deprecation lifecycle. Out-of-scope: model quality evaluation (benchmarks/evals), pricing changes, or new runtime kernels.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A machine-parseable compatibility schema (JSON) is defined with fields described below and a short validator spec.
A2: Intake form updated to require the new compatibility JSON for community models; missing fields block admission.
A3: Runtime team confirms that the schema covers the signals needed for kernel selection and quantization warnings (eng sign-off PR merged)
A4: Pinning policy is documented: when to hard-pin to major.minor, when to soft-pin, and when unpinned variants are allowed; examples included.
A5: Onboarding playbook contains a 'fast fail' checklist and a 3-step rollout (canary, staged, full) with automated sanity checks defined.
A6: QA checklist and automated CI checks exist and run during ingestion. Intake pipeline rejects entries failing the sanity tests with actionable error messages.
compatibility_schema_summary: Proposed minimal fields: runtime_flags (list), kv_cache_compat (boolean), max_sequence_length (int), quantization_profile (enum: fp32|int8|q4_0|q4_1|nf4), required_kernels (list), stateful_attention_variant (string or null), memory_pressure_hint (low|medium|high), affinity_suggestions (cpu|gpu|tpu), sample_inference_payloads (list of small prompt IDs). Each field must include a short justification and a sample inference command. The schema must be machine-validated by intake CI.
pinning_policy_summary: Default: community models are soft-pinned to major.minor for hosted catalog entries (automatic minor upgrades allowed after sanity suite passes). Hard pinning to exact patch is required when runtime_flags include experimental kernels or when memory_pressure_hint is 'high'. Soft-pinning can be lifted after two successful production cycles and a passing regression eval suite. All pin changes must be recorded in the catalog entry's changelog with a reason and risk level.
automation_and_tests: Intake CI will run: a lightweight inference smoke test (sample prompts), profile run (top-5 kernel usage and peak memory), quantization compatibility check (if quantization_profile != 'fp32'), and latency SLO estimation using synthetic load. Results are stored as artifacts and surfaced to the onboarding UI.
rollout_plan: 1) Paper review: PM + Runtime + Security sign-off on schema (this ticket). 2) Implement intake validator in catalog ingestion pipeline (ENG). 3) Update intake form UI and developer docs (Docs). 4) Pilot: onboard two low-risk community models with full schema and run pilot for 2 weeks. 5) Iterate and allow broader ingestion after fixes.
qa_checks: Smoke inference passes within expected latency envelope for at least one sample payload.
Memory peak < 1.2x estimated memory_pressure_hint for target hardware.
No use of unsupported kernels on target runtime (validator detects kernel names).
Quantization emulation matches float baseline within defined divergence threshold for provided prompts.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Requiring too many fields will increase onboarding friction and slow adoption. Mitigation: start with a conservative minimal schema, make additional fields recommended, not required, for first 6 weeks. Risk: false negatives in validator. Mitigation: add an 'allow-list' override for trusted submitters and require a short justification.
